column1: # REDACTED, DEAD, RESERVED, INCOMPLETE AND BROKEN -- the source for Garbage.txt.

#   dead        nothing reaches it; remove it

#   incomplete  works partially; finish it
#   broken      wrong behaviour; fix it, do not remove it

column1: Stmt::Deferred / `:=`
column3: The deferred-binding syntax parses and runs, but evaluates EAGERLY -- the interpreter's handler is a stopgap, self-described at IMPL.md:2993 as "eager in M2; the fusing planner is a later milestone". So a program using `:=` gets correct answers with none of the fusion the syntax promises. Not a bug to file and not a feature to redact: it is M4 work that is partly landed. Re-check: grep -n 'eager in M2' IMPL.md.

column1: Unit handling: scalar rejects what vector accepts
column3: CONFIRMED 2026-09-11 against the master-vintage binary (relocated-session, HEAD 3cca8198, 0 ahead/0 behind; date any binary with `qu eval "tic(1)"` -- it must suggest help("tic"), not available("tic")). CORRECTED after agent_co (Codex) caught an error in the first version of this row: I had written that abs STRIPS the unit from a vector. It does NOT -- the tag survives. Verified: print("{abs([1 ohm, -2.5 kohm])}") => [1, 2500] Ohm. My original probe used print(...) and saw [1, 2500], which is a DIFFERENT defect, recorded separately below. The real inconsistency is scalar-vs-shape-vs-arity: abs(9 ohm) errors "cannot apply the operation to unit" while abs on a unit VECTOR works and keeps the tag; sin(9 ohm)=>0.412118, exp(1 ohm)=>2.718282, log(9 ohm)=>2.197225, sqrt(9 ohm)=>3 all unwrap the same scalar; max(9 ohm)/min(9 ohm)/mean(9 ohm) error "expected a numeric vector, found unit" while max([9 ohm])=>9, sum([9 ohm])=>9, max(9 ohm, 10 ohm)=>10 succeed. Note abs is stricter in the one case where strictness is LEAST justified: abs of a resistance is a resistance, sin of a resistance is dimensionally meaningless and currently succeeds. Silent scalar unwrapping is documented (docs/design/physical-units.md phase 2); this inconsistency is not. Ahmed to choose the rule -- precedent is his "1 V == 1 is no" ruling.

column1: print(v) and "{v}" disagree on unit vectors
column3: FOUND 2026-09-11 while checking Codex's correction; this is what made me misreport the row above. Two render paths give different answers for the SAME value. Scalars agree: print(1 ohm) => 1 Ohm and print("{1 ohm}") => 1 Ohm. Vectors do not: print([1 ohm, 2 ohm]) => [1, 2] but print("{[1 ohm, 2 ohm]}") => [1, 2] Ohm. Not specific to ohms or to abs -- print([1 s, 2 s]) => [1, 2] versus "{...}" => [1, 2] s. So print() silently drops the unit for vectors while keeping it for scalars, and string interpolation keeps it for both. The consequence is worse than cosmetic: it makes unit loss LOOK like it happened when it did not, which is exactly how the row above got written wrong.

column1: zeros/ones silently drop dimensions beyond the second
column3: FOUND by agent_co (Codex) P04/P10, CONFIRMED 2026-09-11 on the master-vintage binary. size(zeros(2,3,4)) => [2, 3]; size(zeros([2,3,4])) => [2, 3]; size(ones(2,3,4)) => [2, 3]. The third dimension is discarded in silence -- no error, no warning, a plausible-looking wrong shape. Fractional sizes are also accepted: size(zeros(2.5,3)) => [2, 3]. Codex traces it to shape_args marking ALL arguments read while consuming only two, which is why the kwarg/arity validation added recently does not catch it. Codex also reports higher-dimensional MAT imports flatten dimensions (source-only, not run here). This is the silent-wrong-answer class, not a missing feature: rejecting invalid rank and fractional sizes is a small fix and must not wait for a general N-D redesign.

column1: plot() silently discards a string y-series and plots the row index
column3: FOUND by agent_q, CONFIRMED 2026-09-11 on the master-vintage binary. plot([1,2,3], ["a","b","c"]) SUCCEEDS -- "plot: figure 1 (3 points)" -- and plots the row index 0..n-1 as y, discarding the data entirely. The same call with the strings in X is correctly rejected: plot(["a","b","c"], [1,5,9]) => "expected a numeric vector; this list holds string at position 0". So validation is asymmetric between the two arguments. Proof the data is gone: plotting ["a","b","c"], ["1","5","9"] and ["z","z","z"] each to SVG gives three BYTE-IDENTICAL files (md5 5c151fcf75a98aafd065c9871c379c62, 8110 bytes each). The reader sees a clean line and has no signal that none of their data was plotted. Documented contract is numbers -- book/src/stdlib/plotting.md line 517. Re-check: qu eval "plot([1,2,3], [\"a\",\"b\",\"c\"])" then compare savefig output across different string data. This is the worst class in the file: not an error, not a missing feature, but a plausible figure containing none of the input.
